q: Does chromatin-loop topology (Rouse/TAD-constrained polymer dynamics vs. free 3-D sub-diffusion) change which pathway-choice scenario best fits repair kinetics, and could it explain 'entwinement' mechanistically rather than as an imposed 25 nm encounter kernel?
basis: The DaMaRiS model imposes CTRW sub-diffusion in a homogeneous 2.5 um nuclear sphere with a fixed 25 nm reactive radius. Real DNA is loop-anchored to cohesin/CTCF-defined TAD boundaries; two DSBs on the same loop have very different encounter statistics than two DSBs on distant loops. The paper does not test alternative polymer/encounter kernels or vary the encounter radius, so 'entwinement' is a modelling choice rather than a physical inference.
next_steps: 1) Reimplement the mean-field surrogate here with a Rouse-polymer inter-DSB distance distribution (analytical closed form: <r^2> ~ N^(1/2) segment number) and re-rank Scenarios A-D. 2) On free ANL uicgpu A100, run a proper Geant4-DNA + polymer chromatin CTRW for one scenario (D) and one alternative (Rouse-loop), 100 nuclei each, compare residual-DSB kinetics + mis-rejoin distance distributions. 3) Vary encounter radius 10/25/50 nm and check if Scenario B/C/D ranking is preserved. 4) Cross-check against Arnould et al. 2021 Hi-C-informed DSB clustering datasets.

q: How does the entwined-vs-competitive model prediction change at high LET (>10 keV/um alpha, carbon ions) where alt-EJ / MMEJ becomes a significant competing pathway that DaMaRiS does not represent?
basis: The paper's fit is at 34 MeV proton, 1.77 keV/um LET, where NHEJ dominates and HR is the main backup. At high LET, complex clustered DSBs shunt to alt-EJ (Pol theta / MMEJ) and to slow processive resection pathways not in the DaMaRiS pathway graph. The four-scenario topology may not be identifiable at high LET because a missing pathway is a strong confounder.
next_steps: 1) Add a fifth pathway state (alt-EJ) to code/damaris_pathway.py with published Pol-theta kinetics (Ceccaldi 2015, Wood 2016). 2) Re-run scenario comparison at 5 keV/um and 100 keV/um LET, using published Frankenberg-Schwager high-LET foci-vs-time data (Asaithamby 2011, Reindl 2015) as the reference. 3) Test whether Scenario D remains best or whether an 'entwined + alt-EJ' hybrid wins at high LET. Free on ANL uicgpu A100 + CELS.

q: Do the four pathway scenarios make distinguishable predictions about *complex* chromosome aberrations (multi-break translocations, ring chromosomes, insertions) rather than just residual-DSB kinetics, and could mFISH/PCC data resolve them?
basis: Residual-DSB counts (gamma-H2AX foci) measure repair *completion* but not *fidelity*. The paper's entwined mechanism specifically predicts particular inter-DSB mis-rejoin statistics -- exactly the observable that would be diagnostic. mFISH karyotyping and premature-chromosome-condensation (PCC) assays yield aberration spectra (dicentrics, translocations, complex exchanges) that the four scenarios should predict differently. This test is not attempted in the paper.
next_steps: 1) Modify the Gillespie simulator to record which DSB-end joins which DSB-end (not just fate). 2) Compare against published mFISH aberration spectra from Loucas & Cornforth 2001, Anderson 2002, Suzuki 2006 (all publicly tabulated). 3) Rank scenarios A/B/C/D by aberration-spectrum log-likelihood, independent of foci-kinetics fit. 4) If D is not uniquely best, quantify how strong an aberration-frequency measurement would need to be to distinguish D from A.

q: Is the pathway choice cell-cycle-phase-dependent in a way that changes the entwined-vs-competitive conclusion? The paper is G2-synchronised, but S-phase and G1 have very different HR/NHEJ competence.
basis: Beucher 2009 chose G2 to see both NHEJ and HR active simultaneously. In G1 (HR unavailable) the four scenarios collapse to NHEJ-only differences; in S-phase, replication-associated DSBs use single-ended HR with different kinetics. The paper's conclusion that 'entwinement is necessary' may not generalise to other cell-cycle phases where the branching topology is genuinely different.
next_steps: 1) Extract cell-cycle-phase-resolved foci-kinetics data from Riballo 2004, Beucher 2009 (G1/S/G2 breakdown), Kuhne 2004. 2) Re-fit A/B/C/D per phase, allowing HR-branch rates to be phase-dependent. 3) Determine whether Scenario D remains uniquely best in G1 (where entwinement should be least active, HR unavailable) -- a strong test of the mechanistic claim. Free run on any CPU.

q: Does the entwined model retain predictive power in NHEJ-defective cancer cell lines (e.g. Artemis-null, DNA-PKcs kinase-dead, Lig4-hypomorphic tumours) that are of therapeutic interest for synthetic-lethal DNA-damage-response inhibitor combinations?
basis: The paper validates against normal fibroblasts and MEFs with clean single-gene knockouts. Cancer cells accumulate multiple partial DDR defects (e.g. ATM-low + BRCA1-hypomorphic + Ku-overexpressing) that create very different pathway competition landscapes. A model that fits normal cells may fail to predict repair phenotypes of BRCA-mutated tumours treated with PARP inhibitors or DNA-PK inhibitors -- a translational gap.
next_steps: 1) Curate a small (5-10 cancer cell line) panel with published DDR-mutation status and foci-vs-time data (DepMap + CCLE + individual papers). 2) Re-fit Scenario D with each DDR gene's activity as a per-line multiplier on the relevant rate constant. 3) Test whether D uniquely predicts observed sensitivity to a DDR-inhibitor panel (PARPi, ATRi, DNA-PKi) vs A/B/C. 4) If D outperforms, that is a strong translational validation; if not, that is a real limit on the paper's claim of mechanistic generality. Free run via depmap skill + CELS oss120/nemotron for parameter sweeps.
